revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is Temple & Webster's total online sales of furniture, homewares and home-improvement products.

For TPW: Revenue grew from A$72.6m (FY2018) to A$664.6m (FY2026), driven by online penetration, category expansion and share gains to ~2.9%. Management targets $1bn+.

What to watch:

  • FY27 opened with checkout revenue down ~13% in the first 7 weeks against a +28% comp
  • No formal FY27 revenue guidance was given

grossMargin.title: Gross Margin
grossMargin.content:
Gross Margin = Gross Profit / Revenue.

For TPW: a presentational break at FY2023 (shipping reclassified into COGS) drops reported GM from ~45% to ~33%. Compare FY2023+ periods to each other only.

ebitdaMargin.title: EBITDA Margin
ebitdaMargin.content:
EBITDA margin on the statutory definition (PBT + D&A + lease interest − interest income).

For TPW: FY27 guidance is a 5-6% underlying margin; the FY26 statutory margin was 3.3%.

underlyingEbitda.title: EBITDA before significant items
underlyingEbitda.content:
Management's underlying measure excludes significant items (NZ start-up, warehouse transition, FX).

What to watch: the gap between statutory and underlying — recurring 'one-offs' are a yellow flag.

fcf.title: Free Cash Flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF = operating cash flow − capex. Owner FCF further deducts SBC, interest income and lease principal.

For TPW: FY2024-25 reported FCF was flattered by negative working capital as revenue grew; FY2026 owner FCF was negative.

netCash.title: Cash Balance
netCash.content:
TPW carries no debt, so cash is net cash (leases excluded).

What to watch: the pace of buybacks against a negative owner-FCF year.

balanceSheet.title: Equity vs Liabilities
balanceSheet.content: Liabilities are mostly trade payables and deferred revenue — the negative working-capital model.

sbc.title: Share-Based Compensation
sbc.content: SBC is a real cost deducted from owner FCF; the share count is held flat because buybacks absorb issuance.

cac.title: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)
cac.content:
CAC is what it costs to win one new customer.

For TPW: this is the company's own disclosed series, read from the FY2024 and FY2025 annual reports: A$43 (FY19), 46, 58, 69, 72, 88, and A$101 (FY25). It has more than doubled in six years.

Temple & Webster defines CAC as total marketing spend × ~75% (their estimate of the share aimed at new rather than repeat customers) divided by the number of first-time customers. Neither input is in this dataset — the new-customer share is a management estimate that moves year to year (74% in FY24, 75% in FY25), and first-time customer counts are only published inside a chart image. So this series is captured as disclosed, not recomputed.

What to watch:

  • Whether rising CAC is offset by higher repeat-order share — repeat customers cost far less to serve
  • FY2026 CAC was not disclosed in the FY26 annual report
  • Marketing ROI fell from 2.0x (FY22/FY23) to 1.4x (FY25)

activeCustomers.title: Active Customers
activeCustomers.content:
Active customers are unique customers who transacted in the last twelve months (LTM).

For TPW: 271k (FY2019) → 1,333k (FY2026). But it is a stock, not a flow: the year-on-year change is net adds (new customers minus lapsed ones), which is why FY2023 shows a decline (941k → 832k) even though the company still acquired new customers that year.

What to watch: growth decelerated from ~40% to 4.6% in FY2026 while marketing spend kept rising — that combination is the core bear argument.

marketing.title: Marketing Spend & Intensity
marketing.content:
Total marketing expense, and the same figure as a share of revenue.

For TPW: spend rose from A$11.1m (10.9% of revenue) in FY2019 to A$101.2m (15.2%) in FY2026. Management has stated a long-term goal of getting below 11% of revenue.

What to watch: marketing intensity is the swing factor in the EBITDA margin. The FY27 guide of a 5-6% underlying margin implicitly assumes this ratio falls.

Half-year rows exist only to H1 FY2022, so the FY/H1 toggle on this chart covers the early years alone.

marketingPerCustomer.title: Marketing Spend per Active Customer
marketingPerCustomer.content:
Total marketing expense divided by LTM active customers.

This is a proxy, not the disclosed CAC. TPW's CAC counts only the new-customer share of spend against first-time customers; this divides all marketing by all active customers. It moves with CAC but is not equal to it — compare the CAC chart above for the company's own figure.

For TPW: roughly A$41 per active customer in FY2019 rising to A$76 in FY2026 — the same direction as disclosed CAC, which is the useful signal.

Why not marketing per net-new customer? Because active customers are a stock, that denominator collapses toward zero when growth slows and goes negative in a year like FY2023. It would have implied a ~13x cost spike in FY2026 against a real figure that is roughly flat — a plausible-looking number that is simply wrong.

orders.title: Total Orders
orders.content:
Total customer orders placed in the period (excludes gift cards and test orders).

For TPW: 1.03m (FY2021) → 1.78m (FY2025). Repeat orders grew faster than new ones and reached 59% of the total in FY2025, up from 44% in FY2019.

What to watch: a rising repeat share is what would let marketing fall back toward the 11%-of-revenue goal.
